prompt: A PI Point data reference uses the tag pattern %Element%LI.PV. On element Tank02, which tag does it resolve to?
explanation: %Element% is replaced by the element name, so %Element%LI.PV on Tank02 becomes Tank02LI.PV. This is the workbook's own example.

prompt: Which are built-in AF data reference types listed in AVEVA training? Select all that apply.
explanation: The workbook lists PI Point, PI Point Array, Formula, Table Lookup, String Builder and URI Builder; <None> means a static value. SQL Query and Excel Link are not built-in DR types.

prompt: What is the default PI Point naming rule AF uses when it creates tags for attributes?
explanation: The default naming rule for created tags is %Element%.%Attribute%.%ID%. One Analysis Service lab suggested %Database%_%Element%.%Attribute% for analysis outputs, but that is a lab setting, not the default.

prompt: Match each substitution to what it refers to.

pairs.right: Attribute Transformer ID on the containing element
Attribute Site ID on the parent element
The default PI Data Archive server

explanation: %@...% substitutes another attribute's value; | points to an attribute on the containing element and ..\ moves up to the parent. %Element% is the element name and %Server% the default Data Archive.

prompt: Why can a Formula data reference attribute used as an analysis input cause performance problems?

options.text: It writes a PI tag on every evaluation
It is computed on demand each time it is read
It disables caching of all inputs

explanation: Formula DR attributes are computed on demand, so feeding them into analyses adds computation each time. Formula DRs are also not time-weighted.

prompt: In a Table Lookup data reference, what does the @ in MaterialID = @Product mean?

options.text: A SQL parameter that must be typed at run time
The value of the attribute named Product

explanation: @ references an attribute value. The lookup returns the row whose MaterialID equals the current value of the Product attribute.

prompt: Which Table Lookup ConfigString option sets the replacement value returned when the query finds no rows? (Give the three-letter key.)
explanation: Appending ;RWM=<value> sets a replacement value when no rows match, for example ;RWM=%Time% or ;RWM=@Attribute2.

prompt: What is the most likely fix?
scenario: A Table Lookup attribute reads from a linked table that has a Timestamp column. Every value it returns carries the timestamp 1/1/1970, so trends look wrong.

options.text: Change the attribute value type to DateTime
Enable "Table provided time series data" and choose the Timestamp column as the time column
Switch the attribute to a Formula reference

explanation: In AF 2.5+, "Table provided time series data" with a chosen time column makes each returned value carry its row's timestamp. Without it, values came back stamped 1/1/1970.

prompt: True or false: an Analysis Data Reference output, trended in a client, follows the analysis's periodic schedule.
explanation: False. Analysis DRs are computed only when a client asks for data. A trended Analysis DR was seen to evaluate at every input event and ignore the periodic schedule; AVEVA staff called it a known issue and recommended a PI Point output.

prompt: After configuring PI Point data references on a template, how do you create the PI tags for all elements in PSE?

options.text: Run piconfig on the Data Archive
Right-click the Elements root and choose Create or Update Data Reference
Export to XML and import again

explanation: Right-click the Elements root and choose "Create or Update Data Reference". The attributes then show "Pt Created". In code, AFDataReference.CreateConfig does the same in bulk.

prompt: Write the event frame attribute PI Point DR config that takes the average of the referenced element's Outlet Temperature over the event frame.
explanation: Event frame attributes reference the primary element with .\Elements[.]|<attribute>, and ;TimeRangeMethod=Average aggregates over the frame's time range. Maximum and StartTime are other methods seen in labs.

prompt: True or false: AF will convert between a PI Point in psi and an attribute in bar because both are pressure units.
explanation: True. AF converts between a PI Point and an attribute (or two attributes) when both units are in the same UOM class. A lab maps a psi tag (Source Units) to an attribute whose default UOM is bar.
